Ban Chang is a relaxed coastal town and district in [Rayong Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ban_Chang_district) , eastern Thailand , known for Phala Beach , local charm, and proximity to U-Tapao Airport.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ban_Chang_district) [[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ban_Chang_district)[[2]](https://mapy.com/en/?source=osm&id=14845628)[[3]](https://www.agoda.com/ban-chang/maps/rayong-th.html)

Geography and Beaches

- **Phala Beach** : Western beach area with quiet sand and seafood spots.
- **Phayun Beach** : Central coastal stretch popular for local relaxation.
- **Nam Rin Beach** : Longest eastern beach featuring open views and eateries.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ban_Chang_district) 

Travel and Location

- **Access** : Roughly a 30 to 45-minute drive from Pattaya.

items.title: Where is the Ban Chiang Archaeological Site?

expanded_element.title: Ban Chiang Project | Research - Penn Museum
expanded_element.description: The Metal Age village and mortuary site of Ban Chiang is in the province of Udon Thani in northeastern Thailand. The Ban Chiang Archaeological Site is a large, prehistoric earthen mound encompassing both residential and mortuary areas.

items.title: What makes Ban Chiang pottery unique?

expanded_element.title: Ban Chiang Pottery: From Prehistoric Civilization to Modern Charm
expanded_element.description: For Thais and ceramic enthusiasts everywhere, the name Ban Chiang (บ้านเชียง)conjures up an image of uniquely painted pottery. The red pattern, which later became known as the “Ban Chiang Rope”, characterizes the clay jars that are around 5,000-7,000 years old, and, perhaps, some of the oldest in the world.

items.title: What is Ban Chiang known for?

expanded_element.title: Ban Chiang Archaeological Site
expanded_element.description: Ban Chiang is considered the most important prehistoric settlement so far discovered in South-East Asia. It marks an important stage in human cultural, social and technological evolution. The site presents the earliest evidence of farming in the region and of the manufacture and use of metals.

items.title: What artifacts were found in Ban Chiang?

expanded_element.title: Ban Chiang Culture | Anthropology | Research Starters - EBSCO
expanded_element.description: Among the most famous of the Ban Chiang artifacts are its pottery, bracelets, anklets, pendants, and beads. The Ban Chiang culture most likely declined because of incursions from the north by the Chinese as their civilization expanded during the Han Dynasty (206 B.C.E.-220 C.E.).
